name: Key Capture Energy (KCE)
headquarters: Albany, New York, United States (offices: Houston, Salt Lake City)
employees: ~85-100 (company site claims both '85+ in 25 states' and 'over 100' — internally inconsistent)
ownership: SK-owned and in play: SK E&S took majority control Dec 2021 (with a >$1B investment pledge); after the SK E&S-SK Innovation merger (Nov 2024) KCE sits under PassKey Inc., SK Innovation E&S's US green-energy platform. Infralogic reported SK launched a sale process mid-April 2026 (Nomura Greentech advising; alternately framed as a ~$350M capital raise); PassKey's on-record line: 'exploring various strategic options to bring in a financial partner.' No outcome announced as of Aug 2026
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Key Capture Energy is the NYISO first-mover (first grid-scale battery in NYISO wholesale, 2019; two LIPA contracts approved Dec 2024) with 623 MW operating (~580 MW ERCOT + ~43 MW NY) and an 8 GW claimed pipeline — and a striking procurement paradox: despite five years of Korean SK ownership, it has never bought a Korean cell. Its fleet is built on Sungrow (~450 MW cumulative — the incumbent primary supplier via a 390 MW framework from 2021) and Powin (~230 MW — whose Chapter 11 and Dec 2025 liquidation left ~40% of the fleet with orphaned-service risk). It has no public FEOC posture, no disclosed safe-harbored equipment, no Hithium history (whitespace, not a blocker), no new COD since January 2025, and an unresolved ownership process that freezes big procurement decisions. Its concentrated forward demand — LIPA's 79 MW/316 MWh + 50 MW/200 MWh BOOT-style contracts, NYSERDA bulk-storage bids (KCE NY 34, 100 MW/4-hr), and ~700 MW of Michigan MISO projects targeting early-2027 construction — is exactly the procurement window now open.
ecosystemRole: We assess KCE as the most winnable account in Batch B for a price-competitive Chinese vendor on paper — a historically price/availability-driven buyer of Chinese systems with active procurement windows (LIPA, NYSERDA ISC, Michigan) and integrator-failure scar tissue that a well-capitalized OEM with strong warranty backstops can answer — and simultaneously one of the most conditional: the sale process could hand control to a sponsor with its own supplier preferences; a retained SK would have an obvious captive pivot to SK On's US LFP (a synergy trade press notes is publicly unexploited); and FEOC economics bind every ITC-claiming project it builds from 2026. In the relationship web, KCE is also the cautionary integrator-risk exhibit: Powin's bankruptcy turned a supplier choice into a fleet liability, which is why vendor viability now outranks price in its diligence.

productsAndServices.name: ERCOT operating fleet (~580 MW)
productsAndServices.description: Built in three procurement waves: (1) three 9.9 MW distribution-connected units, 29.7 MW total, COD 2020 — Powin; (2) KCE TX 11 (50 MW), TX 12 (100 MW), TX 23 (50 MW) — 200 MW, Powin systems with Mitsubishi Power as EPC/PCS, COD ~2021-22; (3) the Sungrow era — TX 13 (50 MW, Scurry Co.), TX 19 + TX 21 (100 MW combined, Williamson Co., in the Dec 2023 ITC transfer), TX 10 (100 MW/200 MWh, Denton Co.) and TX 15 (100 MW/200 MWh, Grimes Co.), both COD Jan 2025 with the 10% Energy Community ITC adder.
productsAndServices.positioning: An early ERCOT mover whose fleet now skews small/short-duration against the market's 4-hr shift; merchant revenue compression (mild weather, algorithmic competition) is the stated pressure.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Merchant ERCOT with ITC-transfer monetization (two of the industry's earliest transfer deals: 120 MW to Enhanced Capital, Dec 2023; 200 MW in Jan 2025).
productsAndServices.roadmap: No new COD since Jan 2025 — the visible stall the sale/recap process is meant to fix.

productsAndServices.name: New York franchise (the regulatory moat)
productsAndServices.description: KCE NY 1 Stillwater (20 MW, NEC — the first grid-scale battery in NYISO wholesale, 2019, then NY's largest Li-ion); KCE NY 6 (20 MW/40 MWh, Erie Co. — Sungrow BESS, Black & McDonald EPC, union labor, $5.0M NYSERDA bridge incentive). Forward book: two LIPA contracts approved Dec 18, 2024 — 79 MW/316 MWh (Hauppauge/Islip) and 50 MW/200 MWh (Shoreham/Brookhaven), BOOT-style (7-yr initial term + LIPA buyout option or 13-yr extension), pay-for-performance, from a 78-bid/3.3 GW RFP; NYSERDA ISCRFP25-1 bids including KCE NY 34 (100 MW/4-hr, Saugerties, proposed in-service Dec 2030) — awards expected ~Q2 2026, results not yet public.
productsAndServices.positioning: First-mover regulatory equity in NYISO plus deep NYSERDA relationships — the moat peers can't quickly replicate; LIPA's municipal-utility procurement brings Chinese-content optics scrutiny.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Utility BOOT contracts (LIPA), NYSERDA incentives, merchant NYISO.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: NYISO wholesale, Long Island reliability, state bulk-storage programs.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Supplier selection for the LIPA projects (LFP specified) and any ISC awards is unannounced — an active procurement window.

productsAndServices.name: MISO/Midwest expansion
productsAndServices.description: ~700 MW in Michigan alone (Pennfield Township — construction targeted early 2027; Ottawa County — KCE MI 1/MI 2), plus Indiana and Illinois positions; company cites electrification and data-center load growth as the demand driver for the Midwest push. Aug 18, 2026: $300M letter-of-credit facility from Standard Chartered (sole provider) to post development-phase credit support, with NYISO + MISO named as the near-term focus.
productsAndServices.positioning: The growth vector: Michigan's storage targets and MISO's data-center-driven load growth — pipeline claims of 8,000+ MW (site also shows 'over 10,000 MW'; use 8 GW).
productsAndServices.roadmap: Early-2027 Michigan construction implies equipment selection through 2026 — inside the FEOC-governed vintage, with no disclosed compliance pathway.

specs.value: KCE NY 1 (selected 2018); NEC exited the ESS business in 2020 — legacy only

specs.label: Korean cells
specs.value: ZERO Korean-cell procurement found despite SK ownership since 2021 — no LG ES/Samsung SDI/SK On/Tesla/Fluence supply identified; trade press flags SK On's US LFP capacity as an unexploited FEOC-era synergy

specs.value: LIPA 79 MW/316 MWh + 50 MW/200 MWh (LFP specified, suppliers unannounced); NYSERDA ISCRFP25-1 incl. KCE NY 34 100 MW/4-hr (awards ~Q2 2026, unpublished); Michigan ~700 MW (early-2027 construction); no disclosed safe-harbored equipment bank

technicalSpecs.notes: Total fleet MWh undisclosed (~1.15-1.25 GWh inferred). Hithium relationship: none found — whitespace. No public FEOC or domestic-content policy statements exist.

recentDevelopments.headline: KCE places a 390 MW BESS order with Sungrow (ST2752UX, 2-hr) — the framework that made Sungrow the incumbent
recentDevelopments.read: The precedent that matters for Hithium: KCE demonstrably commits to Chinese-integrated systems at framework scale when price and availability win.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess KCE as the most procurement-open account in Batch B on revealed behavior: it built its fleet on Chinese systems (Sungrow framework) and US-integrator-with-Chinese-cells (Powin), never pivoted Korean despite SK ownership, and holds concentrated, dated procurement windows (LIPA, NYSERDA ISC, Michigan 2027 construction) with no announced suppliers and no disclosed FEOC pathway — the classic profile of a buyer that decides late and on terms.

(High confidence) We assess the ownership overhang as the gating condition: an active sale/recap since April 2026 freezes framework decisions, and the outcome forks the account — a financial sponsor likely preserves price-driven procurement (opportunity), while a retained/recommitted SK creates an obvious captive pivot to SK On's US LFP that would squeeze Chinese vendors out of exactly the NYISO/MISO builds Hithium would target (threat).

(Moderate confidence) We assess Powin scar tissue as reshaping vendor selection in Hithium's favor on one axis and against it on another: financial-strength and warranty-backstop diligence now dominates (a well-capitalized OEM with 25-yr warranty structures and a US service footprint scores well), while geopolitical/counterparty risk perception — amplified by LIPA's municipal procurement optics and NY's post-2023 fire-safety sensitivities — scores a §154-named supplier poorly.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the FEOC bind as decisive for ITC-claiming vintages: KCE's transfer-monetization model needs compliant equipment from 2026, and no safe-harbored bank is disclosed — so a Hithium pitch is realistic only for structures that don't claim the ITC or for content engineered under whatever compliant path Hithium can stand up; price alone no longer closes at ~55% effective tariff.

(Moderate confidence) For the Hithium lens: work the account as a timing play — track the sale outcome (Nomura process), the NYSERDA ISC award list (~Q2 2026, unpublished), and LIPA supplier selections as the three tells; engage early with commercial/technology leadership (Joel Vyduna) on the Michigan tranche where construction timing (2027) leaves the widest structuring room; and treat SK On's posture as the single variable most likely to close the door.

relationships.note: The incumbent primary supplier — a 390 MW framework (2021) built ~450 MW of the fleet.
relationships.context:
KCE placed a 390 MW BESS order with Sungrow (ST2752UX, 2-hour) in October 2021 — the framework that made Sungrow the incumbent across the Texas fleet (TX 13, TX 19/21, TX 10, TX 15) and the New York franchise (with Black & McDonald EPC and union labor). The last Sungrow delivery reached COD January 2025 (TX 10 + TX 15, 200 MW/400 MWh, with the second ITC transfer).

The precedent the dossier flags: KCE demonstrably commits to Chinese-integrated systems at framework scale when price and availability win — but its next procurement windows (LIPA, NYSERDA, Michigan 2027) have no announced suppliers, no disclosed FEOC pathway, and an unresolved SK ownership process freezing decisions.

metrics.name: Financings
metrics.actual: $93.3M debt for the 230 MW TX portfolio (CIT/Siemens FS/Rabobank, Feb 2021); SK E&S >$1B investment pledge (2021 — deployment unverified); two ITC-transfer monetizations (Dec 2023 ~120 MW to Enhanced Capital; Jan 2025 ~200 MW, buyer unnamed, values undisclosed); $300M Standard Chartered LC facility (Aug 2026); reported ~$350M capital-raise target via Nomura (2026, aggregator)
metrics.result: LC-financed development rather than construction capital — the visible constraint

financials.commentary: ERCOT merchant softness in 2025-26 (mild weather, algorithmic competition) is the stated revenue pressure; SK Innovation's own balance-sheet stress (battery losses drove the E&S merger) underlies the monetization push. NPM reported a 2022 minority-stake sale to 'Stella Investment' — single-source, unverified.
